source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.211
purpose: Boundary record for this material-intake window: under which conditions the statements hold, which objects/limits/normalizations must be preserved, where recounting would double-count the reused old core, what the author leaves unexpanded, and the literal source defects. No correctness verdict on the author's mathematics is issued and nothing here is a repair.

necessary_conditions.statement: 1 ≤ m ≤ n−1 are integers; the ambient space is R^n, so the codimension n−m is at least 1.
necessary_conditions.note: m = n is excluded everywhere; no codimension-zero or current-theoretic case is treated.

necessary_conditions.statement: The set A is Borel measurable (Theorem 8.4 at 2128; Theorem 8.1 has A ⊂ S Borel at 1991; the abstract says Borel at 149).
necessary_conditions.producer_note: Line 237 states Borelness is assumed precisely 'in order to rule out such examples'. The results are not claimed for arbitrary Lebesgue measurable A, and this distinction carries the Nikodym counterexamples of 190-192 and 261-262.

necessary_conditions.statement: The plane field is Lipschitzian as a map into the Grassmannian with the metric d(W_1,W_2)=||P_{W_1}−P_{W_2}||: Theorem 8.4 assumes W_0: A → G(n,m) Lipschitzian, i.e. defined only on A; Theorem 8.1 assumes W_0: S → G(n,m) Lipschitzian with A ⊂ S.
necessary_conditions.note: No C^1 hypothesis and no condition on the variation of the derivative is assumed; lines 208-211 contrast this with the maximal-function literature. In the 8.4 proof the field is extended to all of R^n 'to be an arbitrary constant outside of A' (2139), which is a proof device, not an extra hypothesis on the statement.

necessary_conditions.statement: The measured sets are A ∩ B(x,r) ∩ W(x) with W(x) = x + W_0(x) the affine m-plane through x with direction W_0(x); the convention is stated at 604-605 and re-stated under the theorems at 1999 and 2136.
necessary_conditions.note: These affine planes are not assumed to be disjoint or to foliate anything; 275-282 explains only that they are locally disjoint in a lipeomorphism sense.

necessary_conditions.statement: The quantitative part runs under the Section 4 package (884-900): E Borel with L^n(E)<∞, E ⊂ U open, B Borel, W_0: U → G(n,m) Lipschitzian, Λ>0, and Lipschitz frames w_i, v_i with Lip ≤ Λ that are pointwise orthonormal and span W_0(x) and W_0(x)^⊥.
necessary_conditions.note: This package is produced from the hypotheses by Proposition 3.8 (locally) and 3.9 (globally Borel); it is not an additional assumption of the published theorems.

quantifier_and_regularity.statement: Theorem 8.4 concludes 'for L^n-almost every x ∈ A' (2133); the limsup is taken pointwise in x and the exceptional set is a subset of A.
quantifier_and_regularity.note: The conclusion is NOT a.e. on R^n, and it says nothing outside A. The Foreword Theorem* (266-273) and Theorem 8.1 do quantify a.e. on larger sets: 8.1 item (3.3) is 'for L^n almost every x ∈ S' (1995) and the Foreword Theorem* item (C) is 'for L^n almost every x ∈ R^n' (271). These sites must not be conflated with 8.4.

quantifier_and_regularity.statement: There is no uniformity in x and no rate: the assertion is a pointwise limsup bound along r → 0+ at almost every point of A.
quantifier_and_regularity.note: This is the sense in which the title says 'density estimate from below'.

quantifier_and_regularity.statement: The 8.4 proof introduces ε_1 > 0 with Z'_0 of positive measure (2159-2163), then 'Choose 0 < ε_2 < 10' subject to (1−ε_1)/(1−ε_2) ≤ 1 − ε_1/2 (2170-2174) and 0 < ε_3 < 1/3 subject to 1 − ε_1/2 < 1 − c(n)ε_3 (2175-2179).
quantifier_and_regularity.note: The literal upper bound '10' at 2170 is recorded as written (see source_notation_points); the constraints actually invoked are (final.2) and (final.3).

quantifier_and_regularity.statement: The family of polyballs C_W(x,r) is used as a density basis for L^n-measurable subsets of U 'because their eccentricity is bounded away from zero' (1973, repeated at 2181).
quantifier_and_regularity.note: This is where the non-Euclidean shape of the balls enters; the balls are products of an m-ball and an (n−m)-ball in the two orthogonal pieces.

quantifier_and_regularity.statement: Proposition 5.15 (lb.1) requires B compact (1460); Propositions 7.5 and 7.6 require A closed (1781, 1930); Propositions 6.3 (upper.bound) and 7.8 (Z.positive) impose only small-diameter hypotheses.
quantifier_and_regularity.note: Dropping compactness/closedness would change the statements; these hypotheses must be preserved in any restatement.

normalization_and_dimension.statement: H^m is the m-dimensional Hausdorff outer measure defined through ζ^m(S) = α(m) 2^{-m} (diam S)^m and H^m = lim_{δ→0+} H^m_δ = sup_{δ>0} H^m_δ, with α(m) = L^m(B(0,1)).
normalization_and_dimension.note: This normalization is what makes claim (2.2) 'L^m = H^m = H^m_∞ on R^m' hold (426); changing it would change the constant 1/2^n.

normalization_and_dimension.statement: The denominator is α(m) r^m, the L^m-measure of a Euclidean m-ball of radius r, so the ratio compares the H^m-measure of the intersection with a full m-ball of radius r.
normalization_and_dimension.note: α is defined once at 402 for every dimension, so α(m) and α(n−m) both occur (e.g. 1637).

normalization_and_dimension.statement: The constant is exactly 1/2^n. In the proof it appears through η(n,m) = 2^{-(n−m)} (2152) and the threshold g(x) < η(n,m)/2^m defining Z_0 (2156), with the same powers reappearing at (final.1) (2167) and at 2223.
normalization_and_dimension.note: The factor 2^{-(n−m)} is that of the Jacobian bound in 5.11 (1313); the factor 2^m is that appearing in the (2+ε_1)^m threshold of (final.1). Both powers are part of the statement and must be preserved. Recorded by location; no derivation of the author is certified here.

normalization_and_dimension.statement: For x ∈ A, the set A ∩ B(x,r) ∩ W(x) lies in the affine m-plane W(x), and H^m there agrees with the intrinsic Hausdorff measure of that plane (claim 2.3, 435-447).
normalization_and_dimension.note: The quantity is thus an m-dimensional measurement inside an affine m-plane, not an n-dimensional one.

normalization_and_dimension.statement: L^n(C_W(x_0,r)) = α(m)α(n−m)r^n and diam C_W(x_0,r) ≤ 2√2 r for the polyballs of 7.2.
normalization_and_dimension.note: Both identities are used repeatedly (e.g. 1911, 1920) and fix the volume normalization of the contradiction.

limits.statement: The conclusion is a limsup as r → 0+ (2131), not a limit and not a liminf; no assertion is made that the density exists.
limits.note: Consistently, the hypothesis form used in the reductio is also a strict limsup bound (2156, 2161).

limits.statement: The auxiliary functional Y_E W is defined by a liminf over j of averages over C_{j^{-1}} (def.Y, 1405), and 5.15 passes through a limsup_j and then a liminf_j (1503-1507).
limits.note: The order limsup then liminf is not freely interchangeable; the chain in 1501-1508 is what the author writes.

limits.producer_statement: The averaging radii in def.Y and in the auxiliary averages are the dyadic sequence j^{-1} (1405, 1426, 1476-1480), not a continuous family.
limits.producer_note: The dyadic index is essential to the liminf definition Y_E W.

core_recount_boundaries.note: The existing H3 reason names exactly 'two rectifiable fibrations and quantitative coarea Jacobian bounds', the selection of 'transverse balls whose nonlinear stripes remain disjoint', the 'near-full-volume lower bound' and the 'exact dimensional density constant'; each phrase maps onto the items above.

core_recount_boundaries.statement: Do not count as independent cores: 5.5 (AC.1, five lines from (eq.10) and 5.4(24.2)), 5.16 (lb.2, statement only), 6.3 (upper.bound, 6.2 with 6.1 at τ=1/2), 6.4 (cor.ub, a choice of δ), 7.6 (lower.bound, a choice of δ and a constant), 3.12 (jac.g, the prose estimate of 607-665), 3.18 (two lines), 5.13, 5.14.
core_recount_boundaries.note: Direct consumers, restatements with a different constant, or standard tools of the same core; a different constant or a weaker form does not create a new candidate.

core_recount_boundaries.statement: Do not count: 3.2 (Hausdorff facts), 3.3 (coarea, cited), 3.4 (Grassmannian retraction), 3.6-3.9 (frame parameterizations), 3.14-3.15 (measurability), 5.3 (Binet-Cauchy), 6.1 (bow tie). Their proofs are short and elementary and their content is classical.

Theorem 8.1 (1990-1997) is a different statement from 2111 and is not an alias, but it contributes no independent H2/H3 load: its proof imports 3.8, 5.5 and 7.8 and adds only a Lindelöf cover (2007) and a Borel partition into small-diameter pieces (2019-2020). The same holds for the Foreword Theorem* at 266-273 and the Foreword corollary at 221-224.
core_recount_boundaries.note: Recorded as distinct_statement_no_independent_new_core rather than as an alias, so that Codex sees the statement exists without being invited to open a second entry.

core_recount_boundaries.producer_statement: 3.19 (nik.set, von Neumann selection plus Lusin) is NOT used in the proofs of 8.1 or 8.4; it only supports the remark at 263 on why Lipschitz regularity of the field is the relevant hypothesis.
core_recount_boundaries.producer_note: A technique not on the path to a proved theorem cannot make that theorem a candidate.

core_recount_boundaries.statement: The article title names a conjecture of Zygmund, but the conjecture itself (195-204) is not proved; only the indicator-function lower density bound of Theorem 8.4 is. The title must not be read as covering every other conclusion of the paper either.
core_recount_boundaries.note: Nothing in this intake may be described as proving the full Zygmund conjecture.

author_unexpanded_or_open.statement: The Zygmund conjecture for square-summable f along Lipschitz line fields (195-204), and Stein's singular integral variant (206-207), are stated as open and are not proved.

The proved statement is a lower density bound for indicator functions ('We obtain the following lower density bound for indicator functions', 212-220); it does not give the differentiation formula for general square-summable f.
The proof of Proposition 7.6 (lower.bound) is 'The reader will happily check that ... suits their needs', with δ and c(n) given explicitly (1944-1951).
The proof of Corollary 6.4 (cor.ub) consists only in setting δ = min{δ_{upper.bound}, δ_{Z.1}(n,Λ,1/2)} (1620).
Corollary 5.16 (lb.2) is stated with no proof environment in the source.
Lemma 3.12 (jac.g) has no proof environment; its proof is the prose derivation of 607-665, ending 'In view of (eq.3), we obtain the next lemma' (664).
The two items of 8.3 (8.3.1 at 2076 and 8.3.2 at 2098) are derived in prose (2079-2096, 2105-2123) without proof environments.
Claim #3 inside the proof of 7.3 invokes 'a standard application of homology theory, see, e.g., [DEP.05c, 4.6.1]' when m < n−1 (1715); that step is external to the paper.
The existence of nearly Nikodym sets is attributed to Nikodym (n=2, m=1) and Falconer (m=n−1) with literature references (805-809); no proof is given in the paper.

Other inputs are cited rather than proved: coarea (449-491; Evans–Gariepy, GMT), the Lipschitz retraction (503; GMT 3.1.20), Lipschitz extension (505; GMT 2.10.43), von Neumann selection (867; Srivastava 5.5.3), Lusin (877; GMT 2.5.3), Dynkin class (752; Cohn 1.6.2), coarea on the annuli (2219, 2227; Evans–Gariepy 3.4.3), the polynomial-zero-set fact (1138; GMT 2.6.5).

The Appendix (71 at 2245-2250, 72 at 2256-2261, with proofs 2252-2254 and 2263-2267) is inside a comment environment (2240, 2268) and is not part of the published article; the author calls both results classical (2243) and gives the second proof only 'for the reader familiar with normal currents'.

The literal upper bound is 10; the only constraint actually invoked is (final.2) at 2173.

source_notation_points.literal: In particular, it follows that $A$ is $\mathscr{L}^n$-negligible if and only if ...
source_notation_points.phenomenon: The abstract states the negligibility equivalence with the a.e. variable x ∈ A; Theorem 8.1 states a three-way equivalence with the a.e. variable x ∈ A in (3.2) and x ∈ S in (3.3); the Foreword version at 221-224 uses x ∈ R^2. The three quantifier sites differ.

non_claims: No proof, hypothesis, endpoint, constant, index range or quantifier was added, completed or corrected anywhere in this intake.
No independent correctness judgment on the author's mathematics is offered; 'materially usable' here means only that the statement and proof spans are located and described.
The article is not claimed to prove the Zygmund conjecture; it proves a lower density bound for Borel indicator sets along Lipschitz fields of affine m-planes with the exact constant 1/2^n.

No claim is made that the source package is compilable: cedram, jepplain+eid, de-pauw.bib and titre-jep are absent, and no compilation, content hash, byte comparison or re-download was performed in this window.
No novelty or literature-position claim is made for any result; the bibliography was not followed beyond the citation sites recorded above.
